name: Pocket Pet
summary: Pulse as a virtual pet in a teal egg keychain: its LCD critter flashes a ‘!’ when checkout gets sick and you press A to roll back.
look: Glossy teal egg device on warm paper, greenish 1-bit LCD with pixel grid, pixel sprites and segment-style mono readouts; a real thumb on the coral A button.

components.name: Egg device
components.role: teal glossy shell with keychain loop; the product as an object

components.name: LCD pet
components.role: Pulse: 1-bit pixel critter with sleep, alert and happy sprites

components.name: Status icons
components.role: ‘!’, Z’s and hearts borrowed from virtual-pet UI

components.name: A · B · C buttons
components.role: physical choice: A = Roll back, B = Acknowledge

components.name: Grey herd
components.role: a row of grey devices = the dashboards you had to babysit

motion.name: Stepped sprite swap
motion.how: pet frames switch at 4 fps (every 0.25 s = 8th note at 120 BPM), exactly like the handheld; no tweening on the LCD

motion.name: Hop & land
motion.how: devices drop 60 px with a 0.1 s squash (scaleY 0.9) on each downbeat

motion.name: Button press
motion.how: A depresses 6 px in 0.06 s, LCD inverts for 1 frame, release on the next 8th

story: Hook: five grey pet devices sleep, beep and show charts under 'How many dashboards did you check today?'. Reveal: a teal egg drops in, the LCD egg hatches, 'Acme Pulse' lands. Proof: the LCD shows the alert pet with '!', CHECKOUT −18%, since 09:42, deploy #2231, and a thumb presses A · ROLL BACK. CTA: happy pet with a heart, 'FIXED IN 6 MIN', 'You ship. Pulse watches.' and Start free.
adapt: Put your product’s key state on a tiny LCD with one pixel character, map your primary and secondary actions to buttons A and B, and use the grey device row for the tools you replace.

references.note: egg-shaped handheld, 3 buttons, LCD icons that signal the pet’s needs

fit.risk: Nostalgia can read as a toy and LCD text is low-contrast; keep the LCD big in the proof shot and use real numbers.
